title: Cloud Service Models: IaaS, PaaS, SaaS 🏗️
description: The Pizza‑as‑a‑Service analogy will stick forever.

slides.title: The Pizza Analogy 🍕
slides.content:
# Managing IT Yourself vs Outsourcing

Imagine you’re hungry for pizza. You have four options:

1. **Make from scratch** (buy dough, oven, ingredients) – On‑Premises.
2. **Take & Bake** (pre‑made dough, you bake at home) – IaaS.
3. **Pizza Delivery** (cooked, delivered; you provide table) – PaaS.
4. **Dine Out** (everything done for you) – SaaS.

Cloud service models work exactly the same way – each gives you a different level of control vs convenience.

quizData.question: In the pizza analogy, 'Dine Out' represents which service model?
quizData.explanation: SaaS gives you a complete application, just like dining out gives you the full experience – you just consume.

slides.title: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) 🖥️
slides.content:
# Virtual Machines in the Cloud

IaaS provides raw computing resources: virtual machines, storage, networks. You manage the OS, middleware, runtime, and application.

**Examples**: Amazon EC2, Google Compute Engine, Azure VMs.

**You control**: the operating system, patches, software.
**The provider handles**: the physical hardware, data centre, networking.

**Pizza analogy**: Take & Bake – you get the ingredients (virtual server) but still need to assemble and bake (install software).

slides.title: Platform as a Service (PaaS) 🧩
slides.content:
# Focus on Code, Not Servers

PaaS gives you a managed environment where you deploy your applications without worrying about the underlying infrastructure. You only manage your code and data.

**Examples**: AWS Elastic Beanstalk, Heroku, Google App Engine.

**You manage**: your application and configuration.
**Provider manages**: everything below – OS, patching, scaling.

**Pizza analogy**: Delivery – pizza arrives cooked; you just eat (deploy code).

quizData.question: Which model gives you the most control over the operating system?

options.text: They all give the same control

quizData.explanation: IaaS hands you the OS – you can patch it, tweak it, break it. PaaS hides the OS from you for simplicity.

slides.title: Software as a Service (SaaS) 🍽️
slides.content:
# Just Use It

SaaS delivers fully functional applications over the internet. You don’t manage anything – not even the application logic; you simply use the software.

**Examples**: Gmail, Dropbox, Salesforce.

**You manage**: nothing except your data (sometimes).
**Provider manages**: everything – from hardware to the application.

**Pizza analogy**: Dine Out – you walk in, eat, and leave. Zero effort.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Shared Responsibility Model 🔒
slides.content:
## Who Secures What?

These models map to the **Shared Responsibility Model**:
* IaaS – you secure the OS, apps; cloud secures the physical building.
* PaaS – you secure your app; cloud secures platform.
* SaaS – cloud secures almost everything; you manage access.

We’ll explore this deeply in the security chapter!
